items.title: Refresh AGENTS.md and keep it in sync with the codebase
items.body:
## Summary

`AGENTS.md` is the main guide agents read before working in this repository, but nothing keeps it accurate. It drifts as commands, flags, helpers, and `make` targets change, and agents follow it word for word.

Example: it tells agents to pass **only** the discussion ID to `glab mr note resolve`. That fails as soon as `--repo` is set, because the merge request is then required and comes first (see https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4192 and https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8404).

## Proposal

### 1. Refresh `AGENTS.md`

Check every instruction against the current tree and fix or remove what is out of date:

- `glab` invocations: commands, argument order, flags.
- Helper and example paths (`internal/cmdutils/`, `internal/testing/cmdtest/`, the canonical example files).
- `make` targets, `lefthook` jobs, scripts, environment variables.

### 2. Keep it up to date continuously

Options, which can be combined:

- **CI check**: parse `AGENTS.md` and fail when it references something that no longer exists:
  - every `glab <noun> <verb>` resolves in the cobra command tree, and every `--flag` is defined on it;
  - every repository path exists;
  - every `make` target and `lefthook` job exists.
- **Review rule**: add a block to `.gitlab/duo/mr-review-instructions.yaml` that asks Duo Code Review to flag MRs that rename or remove something `AGENTS.md` mentions without updating it.
- **Scheduled refresh**: a scheduled pipeline or agent flow that compares `AGENTS.md` with the tree and opens an MR when they differ.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `AGENTS.md` is accurate against `main`.
- [ ] At least one automated mechanism catches drift before or soon after merge.

---
_Drafted with an AI agent (Claude Code)._

items.title: Help shows the wrong argument order for mr note resolve, reopen, update, delete, and draft commands
items.body:
## Summary

`--help` shows the merge request and the note or discussion ID in the wrong order for several `glab mr note` commands. Following the help fails.

```shell
$ glab mr note resolve --help
  USAGE
    glab mr note resolve <discussion-id> [<id> | <branch>] [--flags]

$ glab mr note resolve 2c922708e4b90c6159624570e22ec89bf3286261 4191 -R gitlab-org/cli
  No open merge request available for "2c922708e4b90c6159624570e22ec89bf3286261".

$ glab mr note delete 4073931641 4191 -R gitlab-org/cli
  Failed to get merge request 4073931641: 404 Not Found.
```

The commands actually take the merge request first, which is what the `Use` strings, the `Long` text ("The merge request comes first, then the discussion") and the generated pages under `docs/source/` say. Only the rendered `--help` usage line is wrong.

Affected commands (`Use` strings with an optional argument before a required one):

- `mr note resolve` and `mr note reopen`: `[<id> | <branch>] <discussion-id>`
- `mr note update` and `mr note delete`: `[<id> | <branch>] <note-id>`
- `mr note draft update` and `mr note draft delete`: `[<id> | <branch>] <draft-note-id>`

The parent's command list (`glab mr note --help`) shows the same wrong order.

## Cause

Help is rendered by `charm.land/fang/v2` (v2.0.1). `styleUsage` removes every match of `otherArgsRe = regexp.MustCompile(`(\[.*\])`)` from the usage line and appends the matches after the remaining arguments, so any optional `[...]` argument is moved to the end. The regex is also greedy, so a `Use` with two bracket groups is collapsed into one.

This is unchanged on fang's `main` branch.

## Who this affects

Anyone reading `--help`, and especially agents, which tend to copy the usage line. `AGENTS.md` also gives the wrong guidance for `resolve`; that is being fixed separately.

## Possible fixes

- Fix upstream in fang: keep arguments in their original order, or only pull out bracket groups at the end of the line.
- Workaround in glab: post-process or override the usage line for commands where an optional argument comes first.
- Add a test that renders `--help` for these commands and checks the order of arguments.

Found while working on https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4191.

---
_Drafted with an AI agent (Claude Code)._

items.title: Let glab artifact-registry login write Maven's and sbt's config where the tool actually reads it
items.body:
Follow-up from !3710 ([thread](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/3710#note_3709462370)), agreed with @timofurrer.

`glab artifact-registry login --sbt` writes `~/.sbt/1.0/credentials.sbt`, and `--maven` writes `~/.m2/settings.xml`. Neither location is fixed, and neither tool exposes an environment variable this command can read, so a user whose tool looks elsewhere gets a green check and a build that still authenticates with nothing.

- **sbt**: the global base is `defaultGlobalBase/<binary version>`, overridable with the JVM property `-Dsbt.global.base` from the sbt command line, `SBT_OPTS`, `JAVA_OPTS` or an `.sbtopts` file ([`BuildPaths.scala` at v1.10.7](https://github.com/sbt/sbt/blob/v1.10.7/main/src/main/scala/sbt/BuildPaths.scala)). The `1.0` segment is the binary version, so it is right for sbt 1.x only. On `develop` the default has moved off `~/.sbt` entirely and is env-driven (`SBT_CONFIG_HOME`, then `XDG_CONFIG_HOME/sbt`, then `LOCALAPPDATA/sbt`, else `user.home/.config/sbt`, see [`SysProp.scala`](https://github.com/sbt/sbt/blob/develop/main/src/main/scala/sbt/internal/SysProp.scala)).
- **maven**: `settings.xml` can be pointed elsewhere with `-s`, so the same shape applies.

`--gradle` and `--npm` need nothing here: !3710 honours `GRADLE_USER_HOME` and `npm_config_userconfig`, which are the variables those tools actually read.

## Proposal

One explicit override for the file this command writes, serving both `--maven` and `--sbt`, rather than an sbt-specific knob. It covers sbt 1.x, sbt 2.x and `-Dsbt.global.base` without modelling any of them.

Parsing `SBT_OPTS` was considered and rejected: it covers one of the several places the property can come from and quietly misses the rest, so whether the login worked would depend on how the user happens to launch sbt. That is the same silent failure the writers are built to avoid, only harder to reason about.

## Current state

!3710 documents the assumption instead: `sbtCredentialsPathFor`'s doc comment says it assumes a stock sbt 1.x, and the `--sbt` bullet in the command's help says an sbt that moved its global base does not read that file.

<!-- implementation plan added during 2026-09 backlog triage -->

## Implementation plan

> **Note:** This plan was drafted during an AI-assisted triage of the backlog and has not been validated by a maintainer. Treat it as a starting point: file paths, line numbers, and the approach may need adjusting.

Add one `--config-file` flag that overrides the file `--maven` and `--sbt` write. `--docker`, `--gradle` and `--npm` are out of scope: the last two already honour `GRADLE_USER_HOME` and `npm_config_userconfig` (`internal/commands/artifactregistry/login/gradle.go:105`, `npm.go:19`).

1. **Add the flag.** In `NewCmd` (`internal/commands/artifactregistry/login/login.go`), add a `configFile string` field to `options` and register `cmd.Flags().StringVar(&opts.configFile, "config-file", "", "Path to the file to write (Maven/sbt only). Defaults to ~/.m2/settings.xml for --maven and ~/.sbt/1.0/credentials.sbt for --sbt.")`. `--config-file` already exists elsewhere in the tree (`internal/commands/changelog/generate/changelog_generate.go:128`), so the spelling is not new.

2. **Reject the values that cannot work.** In `options.validate`, return a `*cmdutils.FlagError` when `--config-file` is set and the path is a directory, or when it is a relative path you cannot resolve. Follow the existing message shape: start with `invalid --config-file: ...`, never with the flag name capitalized (see the comment above `validate`).

3. **Warn when it does not apply.** In `options.run`, mirror the `--registry-alias` precedent at `login.go:311`: if `o.configFile != "" && !o.maven && !o.sbt`, emit `o.io.LogErrorf("%s --config-file is ignored outside --maven/--sbt logins.\n", o.io.Color().WarnIcon())`. Silently writing the default path while the user named another one is the same "green check, no credential" failure this package is built to avoid.

4. **Thread the resolved path into the writers.** Change `loginMaven(alias, token)` to take the target path and `loginSbt(registry, token)` likewise, resolving it in `run` as `o.configFile` when set and `mavenSettingsPathFor(home)` / `sbtCredentialsPathFor(home)` otherwise. `loginSbt` already calls `upsertLines(sbtCredentialsPathFor(home), ...)` (`sbt.go:136`), and `upsertLines` creates the parent directory itself, so only the path source changes. In `loginMaven` (`maven.go:148`) replace the `filepath.Join(home, ".m2")` pair with `filepath.Dir(path)` and `path`.

5. **Tests.** Extend `internal/commands/artifactregistry/login/maven_test.go` and `sbt_test.go` with a case each that passes an explicit path under `t.TempDir()` and asserts nothing is written under the home set by `setHome` (the shape `TestLoginGradle` already uses for `GRADLE_USER_HOME` at `gradle_test.go:283`). Add to `login_test.go`: the ignored-flag warning, and the validation error. Updating the existing `loginMaven`/`loginSbt` call sites for the new parameter is mechanical, about 50 lines across the two test files.

6. **Docs.** Update the `--maven` and `--sbt` bullets in `Long`, including the sentence at `login.go:151` that today says an sbt which moved its global base does not read the file, then run `make gen-docs` and commit `docs/source/artifact-registry/login.md` in the same commit.
